topics.title: Projectile Motion
topics.subject: physics
outcomes: Describe the motion of a projectile as two independent motions: horizontal motion with constant velocity and vertical motion with constant acceleration due to gravity.
State and apply the range equation R = (v^2 sin(2θ)) / g for a projectile launched and landing at the same height.
Predict the effect of launch angle on the range of a projectile, identifying that 45° gives the maximum range when air resistance is ignored.

body.text: A projectile is any object thrown into the air that moves freely under gravity, after we ignore air resistance. The key idea is that the horizontal and vertical motions are independent of each other. The horizontal motion has constant velocity (no force acts horizontally), while the vertical motion has constant acceleration, g, directed downwards.

body.latex: x(t) = v \cos(\theta) \cdot t, \qquad y(t) = v \sin(\theta) \cdot t - \tfrac{1}{2} g t^2

body.text: The time the projectile stays in the air depends only on the vertical part of the motion. For a projectile launched from and landing on level ground, the time of flight is T = (2 v sin(θ)) / g. Notice that the horizontal velocity does not appear in this formula.

The range R is the horizontal distance travelled before landing. Substituting the time of flight into the horizontal motion gives the range equation. The maximum range is reached when sin(2θ) = 1, that is, when θ = 45°.

The maximum height H reached during the flight is H = (v sin(θ))² / (2g). Use the simulation below to change the launch speed and angle and watch how the range, time of flight, and maximum height change.

sim.caption: Adjust the launch speed and angle. Watch the path of the ball and read the range, time, and maximum height.

quiz.prompt: A ball is kicked from level ground at 20 m/s. At which launch angle does it travel the greatest horizontal distance before landing back on level ground? (Ignore air resistance.)
quiz.explanation: The range equation R = (v² sin(2θ)) / g is largest when sin(2θ) = 1. This happens when 2θ = 90°, so θ = 45°. Launching straight up at 90° gives the greatest height, but zero range.

quiz.prompt: A projectile is launched at 20 m/s at 30° to the horizontal. Using g = 9.81 m/s², what is the range? Round your answer to one decimal place.
Which two quantities affect the time of flight of a projectile launched from and landing on level ground? (Ignore air resistance. Select all that apply.)
quiz.explanation: Time of flight is T = (2 v sin(θ)) / g, so it depends on launch speed, launch angle, and gravity. It does not depend on mass — all projectiles fall with the same acceleration g when air resistance is ignored (Galileo's result).

quiz.prompt: A projectile is launched at 15 m/s at 60° to the horizontal. Using g = 9.81 m/s², what is the maximum height reached, in metres? Round to one decimal place.
Two balls are launched from the same point at the same speed but at different angles. If both reach the same range, which statement is true about their launch angles?

options.text: The two angles add up to 90°
The two angles add up to 45°

quiz.explanation: Since R depends on sin(2θ), and sin(2θ) = sin(180° − 2θ), two launch angles that add to 90° give the same range. For example, 30° and 60° produce the same range. Only 45° gives the maximum range.
